tools.name: grok_spawn
tools.description: Delegate a self-contained task in cwd to a detached Grok Build collaborator and return at once; keep working while it runs. Grok does not see your conversation: include result, context, sources and file/effect limits. Non-Git directories are normal. Optional worktree:true asks Grok for an isolated tree including native-supported uncommitted context; you inspect and integrate. Optional sandbox requests an exact native profile; omission leaves native defaults in control, with no implicit readonly profile. A brief/worktree is not a security sandbox. Attachments pass exact paths with kind reference or image. A key reuses its holder only for the identical complete original request, normalizing omitted worktree=false and attachments=[]; changed input conflicts, unverifiable input retains the key, and neither launches. Use grok_send to change work. New admissions return agent_id/operation_id; existing returns agent_id/summary, not the answer: wait, inspect actual artifacts and follow up before close. Startup/provisioning diagnostics and returned directories remain readable; never replay uncertain creation or select a looser profile automatically. worker_unavailable with admission none means this server cannot start a worker: follow its action, usually a new session.

task.description: Self-contained brief: purpose, relevant facts and sources, the result you need, and any limits on files or effects. Grok does not see your conversation. A leading /name may invoke a native command, skill or workflow; use one only when its effects are authorized.

cwd.description: Existing absolute physical directory, with symlinks already resolved, in which to do the work; Git is unnecessary unless worktree is requested. The filesystem root, exact account home and protected agent state are refused.

worktree.description: Create a native Grok worktree and work in its corresponding subdirectory. Native copy rules include uncommitted work; nothing is applied back automatically. Omitted or false works in cwd. This is file placement, not a sandbox selection.

sandbox.description: Exact native sandbox profile name to request. Omitted passes no --sandbox flag: Grok resolves its configuration and requirements, which may permit unrestricted execution. Independent of worktree. A requested name is not proof of applied confinement.

path.description: Absolute local path. Runtime admission separately checks canonical filesystem identity, allowed boundaries and file type.

attachments.description: Explicit local inputs with required kind: reference supplies a native resource reference; image supplies image content. No path-only or inferred-kind input. A prose path is not an attachment; admission does not prove consumption.

search.description: Exact native per-turn search overrides, not a network firewall or a requirement to search. Omitted engines and semantically empty objects preserve native settings; null on webSearch or xSearch clears that engine's override. Nested null fields mean absence, not clearing an engine. X dates are inclusive fromDate and exclusive toDate at 00:00 UTC, scoped to native keyword/semantic search.

model.description: Explicit native session model selection, including during active work; omitted preserves the native choice.

effort.description: Explicit native session effort selection, including during active work; omitted preserves the native choice.

key.description: Idempotency key unique to the piece of work. An open holder is returned only for the identical complete original spawn request (worktree omitted=false, attachments omitted=[]; other native omissions stay distinct). Changed input conflicts; unverifiable original input retains the key and admits nothing. Recover a lost response with grok_list by this key or the identical keyed call, never a new key. Use grok_send to change the work.

examples.task: Create comparison.docx from the research in this directory, inspect its rendering, and return the document and findings. Leave source files unchanged; do not contact anyone or publish.

tools.name: grok_send
tools.description:
Act on an existing collaborator. action defaults to follow_up; each action accepts only its own fields:
- follow_up (task, attachments?, search?, resume?): Queue new work in the same conversation. It asks for no cancellation, though Grok's follow-up setting may deliver it at once while a turn waits. resume:true reconnects a disconnected collaborator to carry this new work; it never replays earlier input.
- steer (task, attachments?): Redirect current work without cancelling it: text and images are inserted at Grok's next safe point, or become a priority turn if none comes. Attachments must be images.
- send_now (task, attachments?, search?): Submit priority work; Grok may cancel an ordinary running turn for it (an active Goal is steered instead).
- side_question (task): Ask beside running work without adding a turn; the answer arrives as this operation's side answer.
- edit (task, prompt_id): Replace the text of the queued prompt prompt_id (see the queue record); image inputs are kept, prompts with file references are refused.
- configure (model and/or effort): Change the session model and/or effort, even during work; the operation records which setting applied.
Returns the admitted operation_id; read its effect and the resulting turns with grok_wait.

examples.task: Compare the new document with your earlier conclusion.
Prioritize the operational risks in the current analysis.
Which assumption is most important to your current conclusion?
Compare the same queued inputs, focusing on the deployment decision.

tools.name: grok_wait
tools.description: Wait for collaborators. settled (default) returns once a target stops working, needs attention or becomes unavailable with something new; change returns on any meaningful update. Timeout stops nothing. agents contains only pages delivered within the complete JSON max_chars budget, including the triggering target. Excluded targets keep their entire input cursor; rotate delivered targets behind them. result (default) groups turns/text/text_file, side_answers, attention, files, issues, failed/not-sent/unknown operations, native queue-removal outcomes and background tasks; records keeps the full typed stream. Large records use fragments as in grok_read. Drain has_more with read, then retain each delivered cursor. text_file is complete root text only. Idle means queue observed empty; ready means no work running but queue unknown. Neither proves quality, final files or background completion.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor returned by grok_read or grok_wait; pass it unchanged.

until.description: settled (default): return when a target stops working, needs an answer or becomes unavailable, with something new since its cursor. change: return on any meaningful update.

timeout_ms.description: How long to wait. A timeout returns what is available and never stops the work.

view.description: result (default): status, each turn's text and outcome, side answers, attention, files, issues, noteworthy operations and background tasks. records: the full typed record stream. A cursor keeps the view it was created with.

max_chars.description: Budget for JSON.stringify of the entire aggregate wait result; default 32000. agents contains only delivered pages, including the triggering target; excluded targets keep their complete input cursor. Rotate delivered targets behind excluded ones for caller-side progress. Large records use fragments as in grok_read; no oversized exception. If the host shortens output, retry from previous cursors with a smaller budget.

tools.name: grok_read
tools.description: Read retained output passively in result or records view. Omit cursor to start; pass it unchanged to continue while has_more. Its view/prompt_id stay fixed; omit cursor to change them. records adds raw queue, options, capabilities, all operations and resolved attention. max_chars bounds JSON.stringify of the entire public response, not bytes/tokens. Large structured records appear in fragments {record_id,record_type,offset,json,complete}: concatenate exact substrings of one record_id before interpreting or answering. fragment_reset discards an incomplete obsolete version; replay continues without skipping intervening updates. Fragment frames omit the large summary. Too-small budgets return response_budget_too_small without cursor progress. If a host shortens output, retry from the previous cursor with a smaller budget. Reading never starts, resumes, approves or changes work.

cursor.description: Opaque cursor returned by grok_read or grok_wait; pass it unchanged.

view.description: result (default): status, each turn's text and outcome, side answers, attention, files, issues, noteworthy operations and background tasks. records: the full typed record stream. A cursor keeps the view it was created with.

prompt_id.description: Restrict reading to records of this native prompt; the filter stays in the cursor.

max_chars.description: Budget for JSON.stringify of the complete public result, including its envelope; default 32000. Large records use explicit page.fragments JSON substrings, never apparent partial native requests. Join one record_id in offset order before interpreting it; fragment_reset discards an obsolete incomplete version. A budget below the compact progress frame returns response_budget_too_small without advancing. Host byte/token limits may still shorten output: retry from the previous cursor with a smaller budget. text_file supplies root text only.

tools.name: grok_list
tools.description: List collaborators newest first: open ones by default, closed ones too with include_closed. key narrows to collaborators spawned with that key. Use it to recover an agent_id, then grok_wait or grok_read for output. While page.has_more, pass page.next_cursor with the same filters.

include_closed.description: Also list closed collaborators, whose output stays readable.

key.description: Only collaborators spawned with this key.

cursor.description: page.next_cursor from the previous grok_list call with the same filters.

tools.name: grok_respond
tools.description: Answer a pending request from a collaborator in status attention: pass its request_id and the response object for its method, as shown in the attention record. session/request_permission: {outcome: {outcome: "selected", optionId}} with an offered optionId, or {outcome: {outcome: "cancelled"}}. _x.ai/ask_user_question: {outcome: "accepted", answers: {<exact question text>: answer or [answers]}, annotations?}, {outcome: "chat_about_this" or "skip_interview", partial_answers?} or {outcome: "cancelled"}. _x.ai/exit_plan_mode: {outcome: "approved" (implement), "cancelled" (revise the plan) or "abandoned" (leave planning), feedback?}. _x.ai/mcp/elicit: {outcome: accept, decline or cancel, content?}; elicitation/create: {action: accept, decline or cancel, content?}. Decide within the authority you were given and ask your user only for a decision that is theirs. An invalid response leaves the request pending; a submitted answer is not sent again.

response.description: Native response object for the pending request's exact method, preserved without wrapper tags. Permission uses nested outcome; questions/plans and xAI elicitation use outcome; MCP elicitation uses action. The pending native request validates its applicable branch and offered values.

tools.name: grok_interrupt
tools.description: Stop a collaborator's current turn, like Ctrl-C; queued prompts stay queued. With prompt_id, instead remove that exact queued prompt if Grok allows it. Read the later native operation/queue outcome: removal can mean combination or steering, not cancellation of a turn or its pending attention. Admission alone proves neither removal nor cancellation.

prompt_id.description: Exact native prompt identifier returned by this collaborator; pass it unchanged, without trimming.

tools.name: grok_close
tools.description: Close a collaborator you no longer need, cancelling any running work; read what you need first. Closing deletes nothing: retained output, the native session and any worktree stay, and no change is applied to your checkout. A spawn key is released on close.
